Marta S.: Heads-up 1: Im accepting a transfer to our Dublin office and my tentative relocation date is 2026-09-01. Im due to have my baby in mid-August. What do I need to do about parental leave, payroll, and visa timing?
Rory (People Ops): Congrats, Marta! :tada: Important to coordinate three things: (1) local parental leave rules and Redwood local supplement, (2) payroll/benefits cutover timing, and (3) immigration timelines if your work authorization changes. Looping Ivy (Immigration) and Noah (Benefits).
Ivy (Immigration): Hi Marta 1: moving to Dublin means we need to start the work-permit transfer asap. Typical timeline is 812 weeks for processing, sometimes faster. If your due date is mid-August and travel is planned for Sept, we need to know whether you plan to relocate before or after leave. That affects visa start date and whether you can be paid from US payroll vs Irish payroll for the parental period.
Marta S.: Im hoping to stay in the US for birth and immediate 810 weeks, then relocate. So Im asking to be paid from US payroll for the leave period, then switch to Irish payroll once Im ready to move. Is that doable?
Noah (Benefits): Short answer: yes, we usually allow payroll jurisdiction switch after leave but there are benefits implications. While on US payroll youl remain on US health/dental. Once you transfer to Irish payroll you'll transition to local coverage. We need exact dates to coordinate COBRA or coverage end/start where applicable and ensure no gaps for baby/dependents.
Rory (People Ops): Operationally please submit a Parental Leave request in the HR portal with the planned US leave dates and include a note "international transfer after leave". Also file a relocation intent form so Global Mobility flags relocation and tax teams. We'll add a note for payroll handoff.
Payroll Bot: Automated: For cross-border payroll transitions, submit final US pay period end date and new local payroll start date at least 30 days before transfer to avoid dual-pay cycles. Link: https://hr.redwood.example/payroll-crossborder
Ivy (Immigration): Another doc thing: if you will be out on US leave and relocate after, we recommend starting the Irish work-permit application while youre still on US payroll to avoid delay. We can request earliest possible start date on the Irish permit compatible with your relocation date. Please DM me your passport and visa history and Il scope the timeline.
Marta S.: Great. Any impact on company-paid parental weeks? Will Redwoods US parental package apply when I switch to Irish payroll mid-leave?
Noah (Benefits): Company-paid parental leave is administered by payroll jurisdiction at the time of the leave. If your leave period begins while on US payroll, the US parental policy applies for that segment. If you switch payroll mid-leave, wel pro-rate or transition to local statutory entitlements plus Redwood supplement if applicable. We must calculate on a case-by-case basis.
Rory (People Ops): We'll draft a timeline and a payment plan: e.g., 8 weeks on US payroll at US policy rates, then transfer effective the Monday after relocation and apply local entitlements. Please confirm dates and wel produce an official agreement for signatures.
Ken (Office Ops): On the facilities side: once you relocate to Dublin, let us know if you need lactation room access or childcare resources. Dublin office has a parent room and we partner with local childcare referral services. Il add you to the Dublin parents Slack when youre ready.
Marta S.: Thank you all 1: action items: (1) Il submit Parental Leave with dates 2026-07-15 through 2026-09-15 (tentative), note transfer after leave; (2) DM Ivy passport+history; (3) submit relocation intent form. Any other forms?
Rory (People Ops): That covers the major pieces. Also attach a note if you want PTO applied for any unpaid gap. We'll need the exact pay-period cutoff dates from Payroll to ensure US payroll covers the leave dates you asked. I'll draft the leave+transfer agreement once you submit.
Payroll Bot: Reminder: include pay-period end date in your relocation form to avoid missed payroll.
Marta S.: Doing it now. Appreciate the quick answers and help coordinating across teams.
Ivy (Immigration): Il follow up in DM and start the permit intake.
Noah (Benefits): Il run an estimated benefits transition and share likely premium/proration scenarios once we have firm dates.
Rory (People Ops): Great 1 Thanks everyone. Marta 1 congrats and safe travels in advance! :baby::airplane:
